{"id": "d0395ca3-4460-47ec-9899-5253e1f06dbd", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Good news: nothing to worry about on the operations side — this is a known characteristic of how the AWS Sustainability/Customer Carbon Footprint Tool (CCFT) works, not a regression in your actual AWS usage or energy efficiency.

**Why the number changed**
AWS periodically updates the carbon-emissions calculation methodology (a new `ModelVersion`). When that happens, AWS recalculates *all* historical months under the new model and the console/API only ever shows the current model version for every month — it does not keep the old version's numbers alongside the new ones. That's exactly what you're seeing: all twelve months now report `ModelVersion v3.0.1`, replacing whatever version was live when you first captured 412.7 MTCO2e.

**Did your footprint regress?**
No. The delta from 412.7 → 468.3 MTCO2e reflects a methodology/model recalculation applied uniformly across the year, not a change in your actual workloads, usage, or AWS's actual energy consumption. You said you did no optimization work, which is consistent — if the model hadn't changed, your number wouldn't have moved either.

**Can I pull the figure under the old model?**
Unfortunately, no — not after the fact. AWS's own documentation on this is explicit: "The AWS Sustainability service reflects the most recent model version for every month. You will not see two entries for the same month with different ModelVersion values." Once a model version update happens, the prior version's figures are overwritten and aren't retrievable via the console or `GetEstimatedCarbonEmissions` anymore. The 412.7 MTCO2e you already published is the only surviving record of the old model's output for FY2025 — there's no way to re-derive it today.

The documented path forward is to set up a **Data Export** going forward. That captures emissions at gram-level resolution and preserves a durable snapshot, so if the model updates again you'll have your own archived copy to compare against rather than relying on the console's "latest model only" view.

If it'd help, I can put together a short note for your sustainability reporting file capturing this explanation (old figure, new figure, model versions, and the reason for the difference) — just let me know.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
